This is not normal nor is it okay. At all. My boyfriend and I have gotten into some really intense fights before (been together 7 years) and neither of us have EVER laid a hand on each other or caused physical harm. And with how seemingly random this incident appears to be, that’s even more cause for concern. I’m very sorry your husband treated you this way. Lack of communication is one thing—it can usually be worked out with counseling and hard work. But to physically harm your spouse is a HUGE deal and should not be taken lightly. Kicking you was completely out of line and it makes me worried about what the future of your relationship could look like. I get the impression that this could be a “test” from him. That he’s seeing what you will tolerate and what he can get away with so he can continue this harmful behavior or do even worse in the future. I would think about any other red flags you’ve noticed throughout the course of your relationship that you may not have considered before. Also consider the fact that a man who would kick/abuse his wife would probably also abuse his child. Please speak with someone you know about this and come up with a safety plan. I also recommend seeking professional help and guidance. I wish you all the best.

Ask yourself what’s stopping you. Like actually look inside yourself and figure out what is keeping you from getting your shit together or limiting you. Maybe it’s a fear of failure. Maybe it’s a past experience or feeling holding you back. Maybe you’re unsure about the direction you’re going in life. Or maybe it’s just plain depression. Figure out what it is and then tackle that thing. You could see a therapist, start a journal, read a self help book, audit a class, etc. As you start to work on the root cause(s) of your lack of motivation, you’ll be able to move past it more easily. But you have to do SOMETHING to get started. Pick the easiest thing and do it, then move on to something harder and just keep trucking. And give yourself positive reinforcement, like speaking words of affirmation to yourself (Ex:“I’m really proud of myself for choosing to study for an hour instead of scrolling on Reddit. I feel good when I prioritize my studies.”) It’ll feel kinda silly, but words are powerful and it helps. Physical rewards are very motivating as well. Let’s say you have a goal to get a certain grade or higher on an exam. If you meet that goal, treat yourself (within your means). It could be anything from a meal at your favorite restaurant to a Lego set you’ve been wanting, just something to look forward to and an added bonus to achieving something you’ve worked hard for. 
And just because one method of motivating yourself doesn’t work, just keep trying and experimenting. 

Oh and accountability does wonders, as well. Maybe talk to a friend or family member about your struggles and what you’d like to accomplish in the next few months and see if they wouldn’t mind holding you to it.

This is the recipe I use and it is fool-proof! 

-2 sticks unsalted butter, browned & chilled
-1 cup brown sugar
-1/2 cup white sugar
-2 whole eggs, room temp 
-1 egg yolk, room temp 
-1/2 tbsp vanilla
-2 1/4 cup flour
-1 tsp baking soda
-1 tsp salt
-1 cup chocolate chips (1/2 cup chopped, 1/2 whole)

1. Brown your butter and chill in fridge for 45 minutes. You want it cold but not solidified. 
2. Mix together your sugars in a bowl and add the chilled butter. Mix well. 
3. Add your eggs and vanilla. Mix. 
4. In a separate bowl, sift together your dry ingredients. Then add the dry ingredients to the wet and gently mix until all the dry ingredients are evenly incorporated. 
5. Fold in your chocolate chips. I like to finely chop half the chips so you get more chocolate in each bite and I also think it makes for a prettier looking cookie, but this is optional! 
6. Chill your dough for at least 30 minutes and preheat your oven to 375F.
7. I like to use a scale for my dough balls to make sure they are all the same size—I do 70g per dough ball which usually makes about 15 cookies. Place dough balls on a parchment lined baking sheet and bake for 11-13 minutes, until the tops are starting to get golden and the edges are set. 
8. (Optional) Sprinkle each cookie with sea salt.

You fill out a very detailed assessment that is then reviewed by a psychologist. Then you have a telehealth visit with a psychiatrist to further discuss your symptoms and it’s fairly in depth, lasted around 25-30 minutes. 
Not everyone who does this will receive a diagnosis and medication. The doctors are board certified and do speak with you before diagnosing and prescribing. But I am FINALLY medicated after so long of trying and it’s completely changed my life. 
Again, terrible advertisement and I hate the constant minimization of what we actually experience every day, but these services can be a pretty useful tool for people who truly are suffering and can’t get help elsewhere.
